brief: Yesterday's post-Fed move revived questions about systematic supply, and with positioning fairly neutral, CTA activity carries more weight in this market. SPX was within 1.1% of the CTA short-term threshold as of yesterday's close and is up that amount today. Clearing the threshold would shift GS's near-term CTA estimates and begin drying up systematic supply. CTAs are currently long $37.54bn of US equities (22nd percentile, 1-year lookback), and GS expects today's move to moderate current flow estimates, which model CTAs as sellers of $5.4bn SPX over the next month in a flat tape, sellers of $54bn in a down tape, and buyers of $17bn in an up tape. Dealers are estimated long $3.84bn of gamma at spot (GS desk: 6/10) and are expected to move longer gamma to the topside, 8/10 on a +1% move versus 3/10 on a -1% move, which GS expects to dampen index moves, though underweight investor positioning is a tailwind if macro news turns positive. Gross leverage is elevated at 208.8% (79th percentile, 5-year) while net leverage and the AAII bull-bear spread sit near multi-year lows, and GS expects sentiment to need further repair before meaningful re-risking.
